# Study 1 — Methods (redacted)

## Participants

Sixty undergraduates took part in exchange for course credit. Participants were
randomly assigned to one of two conditions, with equal numbers per condition.
Age was recorded but not used in the analysis.

## Procedure

Participants held a short conversation with a confederate. In the *attention*
condition the confederate faced the participant, maintained eye contact and
responded to what the participant said. In the *control* condition the
confederate looked at a form on the desk and gave only minimal acknowledgements.

## Measures

After the conversation participants rated how close they felt to the
confederate on a single item, from one (not at all close) to seven (extremely
close). This item is the outcome, `closeness`.

## Analysis

We compared mean closeness between the two conditions with an
independent-samples t test assuming equal variances (Student's t test, pooled
variance), two-sided. We report the group means and standard deviations, the t
statistic with its degrees of freedom, the p value, and Cohen's d computed with
the pooled standard deviation. No participants were excluded and there are no
missing values.
